name: Cyberespionage Campaign by Chinese APT Group Cicada Targets Government Organizations, NGOs
description:
Researchers from the Symantec Threat Hunter Team have discovered a cyberespionage campaign that has been targeting organizations in several countries all across the world. The campaign has been linked to a Chinese state-sponsored advanced persistent threat (APT) group named Cicada.

The operation
Cicada, also known as APT 10, mostly targeted Japanese organizations in the past. But the current campaign has targeted government, legal, religious, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in several countries. The threat actors behind the campaign gain initial access to targeted networks by exploiting a vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange Servers. Then they deploy a backdoor named ‘SodaMaster’, which is a Windows-based remote access trojan (RAT) designed to exfiltrate information to its command-and-control (C2) server and deploy additional payloads.
